title: Commitment clauses, contingent remediation ladder, and error-budget allocation for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Purpose: Draft a contract-friendly, operationally actionable SLA and error-budget allocation model for Dedicated GPU capacity that ties committed throughput to a contingent remediation ladder. This ticket produces the canonical language to include in commercial contracts and the internal playbook for computing credits, plus the autoscaling/observability guardrails required to make measurements reliable. Goals: 1) Unambiguous measurement windows and telemetry sources for throughput commitments. 2) A stepped remediation ladder (credits + operational remedies) that scales with outage type (degradation vs. full outage) and duration. 3) Interplay with autoscaling: clearly defined triggers, stabilization windows, and customer-facing credit adjustments when autoscaler behavior (e.g., scale latency or quota limits) contributes to shortfall. 4) Edge cases: AZ failover, customer misconfiguration, force majeure, and model-variant fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Contract clause text (<= 300 words) describing an SLA that maps committed throughput to monthly error budget and a remediation ladder with credit formulas
A deterministic measurement spec listing telemetry sources (ingress QPS, served tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, model variant mapping) and authoritative aggregation windows
Worked examples showing credit computation for 3 scenarios: (a) short transient degradation, (b) sustained under-serve during autoscaler cooldown, (c) cross-AZ failover with partial capacity loss
Defined autoscale interlock: stabilization window, override policies, and how reactive scaling impacts credits
Sign-off from Legal and SRE on wording and metricization (links in attachments)
An internal playbook checklist for CSM/Support to compute and apply credits per contract

example_credit_formula: Definitions: CommittedCapacity = tokens/sec committed in contract. ObservedServeRate(t) = measured served tokens/sec over the 1-hour window t. Shortfall(t) = max(0, CommittedCapacity - ObservedServeRate(t)). Per-window credit (USD) = Shortfall(t) / CommittedCapacity * HourlyCommitmentPrice. Monthly credit = sum(per-window credit over windows that exceed the shortfall threshold). Example: Customer committed 100k tokens/sec at $10k/day (~$300k/mo). One hour observed rate = 70k tokens/sec => shortfall = 30k = 30%. Hourly commitment price = monthly_commit/720 = 300000/720 = $416.67. Credit for that hour = 0.30 * $416.67 = $125.00.
remediation_ladder: Step 0 — Automatic mitigations (no customer credit): prefix caching, model fallback to lower-context variant, burst buffer for up to 5 minutes.

Step 1 — Tiered Credit (short degradation): If shortfall > 10% sustained for 1 hour but < 6 hours, apply proportional invoice credit calculated by formula above. Customer notified automatically at 15 minutes with incident ticket link.

Step 2 — Escalation (sustained): If shortfall persists > 6 hours or shortfall > 50% for any 30-minute window, in addition to credits, schedule a remediation call and offer temporary capacity uplift (subject to availability).

Step 3 — Material Failure (> 24 hours): If commit is unmet > 24 hours and remediation fails, escalate financial remedy up to the lesser of 30% of monthly committed fee or prorated credit for the entire impacted period, plus formal root-cause report and 30-day action plan.
Non-attributable clause: If the root cause is customer misconfiguration, force majeure, or third-party outage outside Redwood control (as defined in the contract), credits are not issued.
autoscale_interlock_spec: High-level: 1) Autoscaler emits event with reason tags (policy, cooldown, quota-limited). 2) Observability correlates events and compute capacity with served tokens to determine attribution. Attribution rules: - If autoscaler was within policy and capacity available but cluster-level quota prevented scaling, credit attributed to Redwood. - If autoscaler policy prevented scaling by design (customer requested min/max), credit may be reduced proportionally. Stabilization windows: scale-up stabilization = 10 minutes, scale-down stabilization = 30 minutes. During stabilization, observed metrics are not considered final for crediting unless degradation exceeds 50% for two consecutive stabilization windows.
worked_examples: Scenario A (Transient degradation): 30-minute blip where ObservedServeRate drops to 85% of commit. Because shortfall < 10% and duration < 1 hour, automatic mitigations apply and no credit is issued.

Scenario B (Autoscale cooldown): Traffic spike increases need from 100k to 300k tokens/sec. Autoscaler begins scale but cluster quota causes a 45-minute delay. ObservedServeRate averages 70% during that window. Credit computed for windows beyond the 10-minute scale-up stabilization and attributed to Redwood because autoscaler was blocked by cluster quota. Apply Step 1 credits for the impacted hours and offer temporary uplift if available.

Scenario C (Cross-AZ partial outage): One AZ loses 40% of capacity for 3 hours; system routes remaining traffic but observed serve rate is 75% of commit. Because this is an infrastructure failure, Step 2 applies with proportional credits and a remediation call. If cause is due to third-party network provider, evaluate non-attributable clause.
contract_snippet_candidate: Service Commitment: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide Dedicated capacity to support the Customer's committed throughput (CommittedCapacity). Availability and throughput will be measured using served tokens/sec over rolling 1-hour windows aggregated from Redwood's authoritative telemetry. If Redwood fails to meet CommittedCapacity for a given window, Customer will be eligible for invoice credits computed proportionally to the observed shortfall as set forth in this SLA. Customer acknowledges a 10% shortfall tolerance for transient events. Credits will be applied to the customer's next invoice and are capped at the customer's total committed monthly spend. Credits are the sole and exclusive financial remedy for throughput shortfalls except where otherwise agreed in writing.
legal_notes: Avoid using 'penalty' or 'liquidated damages' terminology — prefer 'invoice credits' language per Legal guidance.
Cap cumulative credits to monthly committed spend to limit downstream financial exposure.

Include a clause enabling Redwood to exclude periods where the customer has configured restrictive autoscaler min/max bounds that prevent scaling (customer-configured limits must be documented in the Console logs to be considered attributable to the customer).
